The proposed solution is correct. 

To maximize the concatenated number, integers must be sorted in descending order according to the relation $a \succ b \iff \overline{ab} > \overline{ba}$, which is equivalent to ordering by the value of their infinite repeating decimals $0.\overline{a} > 0.\overline{b}$, or $\frac{a}{10^{|a|}-1} > \frac{b}{10^{|b|}-1}$.

Comparing any integer $n$ with $2025$:
- **1-digit ($n \in [1, 9]$):** $n > \frac{2025 \times 9}{9999} \approx 1.82 \implies n \in [2, 9]$ (8 numbers)
- **2-digit ($n \in [10, 99]$):** $n > \frac{2025 \times 99}{9999} \approx 20.05 \implies n \in [21, 99]$ (79 numbers)
- **3-digit ($n \in [100, 999]$):** $n > \frac{2025 \times 999}{9999} \approx 202.32 \implies n \in [203, 999]$ (797 numbers)
- **4-digit ($n \in [1000, 9999]$):** $n > \frac{2025 \times 9999}{9999} = 2025 \implies n \in [2026, 9999]$ (7974 numbers)
- **5-digit ($n \in [10000, 99999]$):** $n > \frac{2025 \times 99999}{9999} \approx 20251.82 \implies n \in [20252, 99999]$ (79748 numbers)

Total numbers preceding $2025$:
$$8 + 79 + 797 + 7974 + 79748 = 88606$$

Thus, $2025$ appears at position $88606 + 1 = 88607$.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
